name: Massive Attack
hook: A Bristol collective that grew out of a sound system and made the album usually called the first trip-hop record.
blurb: Massive Attack formed in Bristol in 1988, growing out of the Wild Bunch, one of the first sound systems started in Britain, so their roots run through the same Jamaican practice as dub itself. Their first album, 'Blue Lines' (Virgin, 1991), is usually called the first trip-hop album. In 1995 they asked Mad Professor to remix a single from their second album, 'Protection', and widened the request to the whole album, which he remade as dub as 'No Protection': the dub tradition invited back into music it had helped shape.

signatureTracks.title: Blue Lines
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The debut album, generally considered the first album of trip-hop.

signatureTracks.title: Protection
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The second album, which won a Brit award for Best Dance Act and which Mad Professor then remade as dub.

signatureTracks.title: Mezzanine
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The third album and their most commercially successful, selling nearly four million copies.
